answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must lock collateral in a shared verification lagoon where registration burns a non-refundable ember of stake. When an agent attempts to forge multiple identities, the protocol imposes superlinear cost scaling: registering the n-th identity requires burning stake proportional to n^2.5. This cryptographic stake burning creates prohibitive economic friction, forcing the attacker's capital expenditure to scale superlinearly beyond any extractable payoff.
